body.en: Python is a high-level, free and open-source language. It is interpreted, so statements are executed one by one. It is case-sensitive (Marks and marks are different names), portable across operating systems, and uses indentation to group statements. Python has two modes. In interactive mode we type a statement at the >>> prompt and see the result immediately. In script mode we save a program in a file with the .py extension and run the whole file.

narration.kn: ಪೈಥಾನ್ ಉನ್ನತ ಮಟ್ಟದ, ಉಚಿತ ಮತ್ತು ತೆರೆದ ಮೂಲ ಭಾಷೆ. ಇದು ಇಂಟರ್‌ಪ್ರಿಟ್ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಅಕ್ಷರ ಗಾತ್ರ ಸಂವೇದಿ (case-sensitive) ಮತ್ತು ಇಂಡೆಂಟೇಶನ್ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಂವಾದಾತ್ಮಕ ಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ >>> ಬಳಿ ಹೇಳಿಕೆ ಟೈಪ್ ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇವೆ; ಸ್ಕ್ರಿಪ್ಟ್ ಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ .py ಫೈಲ್ ಉಳಿಸಿ ಚಲಾಯಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

title.en: On the board: Two ways to run Python, and naming rules

say.en: In interactive mode we type one statement at the prompt and see the result at once.
In script mode we save many statements in a .py file and run the whole file. It can be saved and run again.
Python is an interpreter: it runs one statement at a time, top to bottom.
An identifier may use letters, digits and underscore, must not start with a digit, and must not be a keyword.
Remember that Marks and marks are two different names, because Python is case-sensitive.

narration.en: We compare interactive mode and script mode, then test some names against the rules for identifiers.

body.en: Keywords are reserved words with a special meaning, such as if, else, for, while, True, False, None, and, or, not, def and import; they cannot be used as names. Identifiers are names we give to variables and functions. Rules: an identifier may contain letters, digits and the underscore; it must not start with a digit; it cannot be a keyword; and it cannot contain spaces or special symbols like !, @, # or $.

points.en: Keywords are reserved: if, else, for, while, True, None …
Identifier: letters, digits, _ ; not starting with a digit
No spaces or symbols such as @ # $ - in identifiers

problem.en: Which of these are valid identifiers? total_marks, 2ndName, _count, for, roll no, Avg1

steps.en: total_marks, _count and Avg1 use only letters, digits and underscores and do not start with a digit: valid.
roll no contains a space: invalid.

answer.en: Valid: total_marks, _count, Avg1. Invalid: 2ndName, for, roll no.
